question: Is the reported energy width ordering change attributable solely to different map composition, or does an original-versus-added workload change remain on the same maps?
data: Fixed changed-radius query/map/catalogue outcomes and original primary summaries; no new outcomes, fits or normalisers.
matching: For each domain use all test maps with at least one distinct added crossing mask, as defined by the fixed geometric rules (5Census,124energy); retain every original query on those same maps and all their added queries. No failure/coverage/saturation-based filtering.

comparisons.scope: Original fixed methods; expanded catalogs already exactly coincide with fixed ones. Every comparison uses identical query sets within each map/subset.

outcomes.per_map: Compute each method mean width_ratio within original queries and within added queries using saved query-specific coarse normalizers; contrast d=transport_width-baseline_width. Positive means transport wider.
outcomes.decomposition: Observed difference between added-subset mean contrast and full-original mean contrast = selection component (matched-original minus full-original) + within-map workload component (matched-added minus matched-original). Exact finite-frame accounting, not causal effects.
summaries: Original-full and matched-original/added method mean widths and contrasts; paired mean change.
Paired median and25th/75thpercentile change; positive/negative/tie counts for original and added contrasts; sign-switch counts.
Leave-one-map-out range of original contrast, added contrast and paired mean change; deterministic influence diagnostic.
outcomes.tolerance: Absolute normalized width contrast<=1e-6 is a numerical tie, matching the original comparative count convention.
outcomes.uncertainty: Counts, paired empirical distribution and influence ranges describe these finite reused frames; no iid/external confidence interval, significance or causal identification. No geometry-only attribution: query mix and per-query coarse widths change together.

interpretation: If matched-original and matched-added means retain opposite signs, selection alone cannot account for the reversal. If matched-original already has added ordering, correct the reversal interpretation and identify composition. Retain any mixed/unstable result. Do not search other matches/radii after seeing results.
consolidation: Replace/qualify the existing width-reversal interpretation within current results/conclusion, using a short paired comparison and existing table; no new table/figure/raw-result dump. Stop once this competing explanation is resolved at the descriptive level; broader mechanisms or populations remain optional.
